commit message:
Store minhashes separately from hashes

Keeping minhashes and hashes in the same element of the list that makes
up a TextReuseTextDocument was a mistake. The two are not at all the
same, conceptually. Furthermore, the entire advantage of hashing the
tokens is that the tokens can be discarded. But if one needs to rehash,
the tokens need to stick around or be retokenized, which is the most
expensive part of the process in terms of memory and computation.

This function adds an element `x$minhashes` to TextReuseTextDocuments,
provides appropriate accessor and existence functions, make
functions like `lsh()` only use minhashes instead of hashes, and
rewrites documentation and vignettes as appropriate.

The README is expanded to describe the three main kinds of analysis.

commit message:
Transferred discrete principle curvature functions to mrisurf.[ch]

o Traditionally, the principle curvatures are calculated with:

        int MRIScomputeSecondFundamentalForm(MRI_SURFACE *mris) ;

o To use the new discrete-based code, use:

        short MRIScomputeSecondFundamentalFormDiscrete(MRIS* apmris);

Note that

int          MRIScomputeSecondFundamentalFormAtVertex(MRI_SURFACE *mris,
                                                      int vno,
                                                      int *vertices,
                                                      int vnum) ;
int          MRIScomputeSecondFundamentalFormThresholded(MRI_SURFACE *mris,
                                                         double thresh) ;

still use the traditional (i.e. non-discrete) methods.


-=R

New Class MultiRegistration:
- covers functionality of former mri_robust_template
- cleanup code and output
- bugfix: fixed segfault when -weights are output
- improvements: deals now with -iscale flag for template estimation
   of images with different intensities
- can deal with subsample flag (on low memory systems)
- deals with maxit and epsit flags (to adjust termination criteria)
- added new functionality of --noit flag: if no initial xforms are
   passed, initialize them to inittp (as in the usual stream) and only
   ouput average directly ( --> to be used for simple motion correction)
- default parameter adjustment (speed up!):
  -- max 6 global iterations, terminate with eps: 0.03 transform change
  -- use accurate reg. to create initial space (reduces global iterations)
  -- do not subsample on first global it., run full resolution directly

commit message:
These three functions are used to solve for a vox2ras matrix given
only a Siemens meas.asc file.

vox2ras_dfmeas	- main function. Accepts a given meas.asc file for
		  processing. Can also accept voxelDimension vector
	          and logicalSpaceSize vector (will make default
		  assumptions if not specified).
vox2ras_rsolve	- solve for the rotation component of vox2ras either
		  by directly parising "enhanced" meas.asc files, or
		  attempting a direct calculation based on a single
	          direction cosine.
vox2ras_ksolve	- solve for the center of k-space. Depends on
		  a vox2ras with correct rotation components.

commit message:
bf: more managed xyz and dist 3 (#612)

*         Change a lot more modifies of xyz to use MRISsetXYZ

        Free the VERTEX::dist in many more places where the dist is invalid, to verify it is being recomputed with the new xyz values

        Use MRISexportXYZ rather than VERTEX::tdxyz in some cases to reduce usage of the tdxyz and get better memory traffic performance

        Add base.h copeWithLogicProblem that allows reporting and optional fixing of possible logic problems in the code

        Move origxyz after xyz in the VERTEX because xyz is the input and origxyz is the output

        Start keeping track of the dist_orig_nsize because changing dist_nsize did not always recompute the corresponding dist_orig values

        Replace calls to the badly misnamed MRIScomputeGeometricProperties with the existing MRIS_facesAtVertices_reorder, because that is what it does

        Passed __FILE__ and __LINE__ into MRISsetXYZ to allow for better warning messages

        Added and used MRISblendXYZandTXYZ   (mris, ...) rather than having multiple copies of the operation   (xyz = a * xyz + b * txyz)

        Added and used MRISscaleThenTranslate(mris, ...) rather than having multiple copies of the operation   (x = ax * x + bx), (y = ay * y + by), ...

        Use mrisComputeSurfaceDimensions rather than having multiple copies of the operation

        Logic errors being flagged
            mris_sphere/mris_sphere.c main()
                is not copying the xyz into the origxyz
                hence is later using zeroes rather than the correct values
            utils/mrisurf_integrate.c MRISinflateBrain()
                is not copying the xyz into the origxyz

author: Rudolph Pienaar <rudolph@nmr.mgh.harvard.edu>
commit message:
Added --label <labelFile> handling.

        If specified, constraint the calculation to the vertices defined in
        the <FreeSurferLabelFile>. This is most useful for calculations
        relating to curvature and thickness files that are defined on a
        surface.

        Note that 'mris_calc' will apply a specified label filter to any
        inputs, i.e. surface related measures (thickness, curvatures) *and*
        volumes, if volumes are input. This means that if a surface label is
        applied to a volume, the corresponding volume indices will be tagged
        and used for calculations. Applying such a surface filter operation
        to volume indices might be somewhat meaningless.

        Also, if a label is specified, calculations outside of the label
        area are set to zero. That means if an addition operation is
        specified, only the input indices corresponding to the label will
        be operated on. The non-label indices in the output will be zero.

commit message:
Previously 'mris_calc' operated on two inputs:

	<input1> <ACTION> <input2>

There are cases where only

	<input1> <ACTION>

can be useful (e.g. in querying properties of <input1>). Several
such single input functions have been added. These do not create
output curvature files, but print information about <input1> to
stdout:

        ACTION  INPUTS OUTPUTS                  EFFECT
          size     1      0     print the size of <curvFile1>
          min      1      0     print the min value (and index) of <curvFile1>
          max      1      0     print the max value (and index) of <curvFile1>
          mean     1      0     print the mean value of <curvFile1>
          std      1      0     print the standard deviation of <curvFile1>
          stats    1      0     process 'size', 'min', 'max', 'mean', 'std'

commit message:
mris_label2annot
  1. introduce --do-unknown-stat option to include the "unknown" when computing the maxstat winner
     the unknown stat is calculated as 1 - sum(all-other-label-stat)
  2. don't apply LabelThresh if --do-unknown-stat is true
  3. 2D labelStat table is implemented using MRI structure (nvertices x (nlabels+5) x 1 x 1) to track labels assigned to each vertex
     col 0 - the final annotation assigned
     col 1 - labelno. assigned
     col 2 - no. of labels assinged
     col 3 - label maxstat selected
     col 4 - calculated unknown-stat [1 - sum(all-other-label-stat)]
     col 5 to (5+nlabels-1) - record all labelno. assigned to the vertex
  4. col 3 and col 4 are used for maxstat and unknownstat determination
     the table is used to report vertices mapped to multiple labels
  5. the option is implemented for label2annotationV2() only

author: Yujing Huang <yhuang43@mgh.harvard.edu>
commit message:
centos9/gcc11, ITK5/VTK8 upgrade
  fix multiple definition errors between libnifti.a and libITKznz.a/libITKniftiio.a in ITK5.4

  1. libutils.a needs the symbols znzeof/znzgetc/znzgets from libnifti.a, which are not exported from ITK5.4 libITKznz.a
     When libITKznz.a is searched by the linker first, libnifti.a will also need to be included for libutils.a.
     This results in multiple definition errors for symbols in both libITKznz.a and libnifti.a
  2. Since ITK5.0, name mangling (prefixed with itk_) is not done for libITKniftiio.a. Symbols from libITKniftiio.a and libnifti.a have the same names.
  3. Since ITK5.3, libITKIONIFTI.a has a dependency on libITKniftiio.a/libITKznz.a - itkNiftiImageIO.cxx in libITKIONIFTI.a references nifty_image_write_status() in libITKniftiio.a
     When an application needs libITKIONIFTI.a, both libITKniftiio.a and libnifti.a will be included because of missing znz symbols from libITKznz.a.
     This results in multiple definition errors for symbols in both libITKniftiio.a and libnifti.a

  One way to fix this
  1. add nifty_image_write_status() and supporting functions nifti_image_write_engine()/nifti_NBL_matches_nim() to our libnifiti.a
  2. list libnifti.a before libITKniftiio.a/libITKznz.a for the linker to search it first.

  Notes:
    1. add linker flag "-Wl,--allow-multiple-definition" will allow multiple definitions and the first definition will be used.
    2. compile ITK with -DCOMPILE_NIFTIUNUSED_CODE should have additional functions exported from libITKznz.a (znzdopen/znzgetc/znzgets/znzputc/znzprintf). But znzeof is still missing.
    3. in ITK5.4, nifti_image_write_engine() replaces nifti_image_write_hdr_img2(), nifti_image_write_hdr_img2() calls nifti_image_write_engine().

commit message:
For each subject, creates a binary volume from the aseg.mgz based on
the segmentation number(s) passed with --seg. This binary volume is
then resliced to talirach/MNI305/fsaverage space using the 12 DOF
talaiach.xfm. The volumes for all the subjects are concatenated
together and the mean computed.  The value at each voxel is then the
fraction of subjects that had that segmentation at that voxel. It can
also be thought of as a probability that the talairach voxel is part
of the segmentation.

commit message:
This GCA was created to perform MRF on the samseg crisp segmentation
to help refine the boundaries. The GCA was created by:

    1. Running the manual seg subjects through v6 recon-all to create the
    orig.mgz (maybe other outputs needed by xcerebralseg below)

    2. Running each orig.mgz through samseg to create the
    bias corrected image, the segmentation, and samseg.talairach.lta

    3. Linking samseg.talairach.lta to mri/transforms

    4. Merging the manual labels (seg_edited10.mgz) with the extacerebral
    segmentation from crispSementation (to create seg+xcer.mgz):

    xcerebralseg --s $s --o seg+xcer.mgz --m seg_edited10.mgz \
        --seg1 samseg/orig_crispSegmentation.nii \
        --srcvol samseg/orig_biasCorrected.nii --no-pons --no-vermis

    5. Train with

    mri_ca_train  -prior_spacing 2 -node_spacing 4 -mask seg+xcer.mgz \
      -parc_dir seg+xcer.mgz -xform samseg.talairach.lta \
      -T1 samseg.m3z $subjectlist $trggca

where samseg.m3z is the m3z created when running samseg.

frontend for a series of programs which will sample a volume to a
surface, smooth on the surface, then replace the surface voxels in the
volume with values that were smoothed on the surface. This can make it
convenient for interfacing volume-based functional analysis tools with
surface-based smoothing. When complete, values not on the surface will
be the same as in the input volume. Both hemispheres are done.

This is a registration matrix that maps the MNI152 to the MNI305
(fsaverage). The MNI152 is used by FSL.

It was created with:

spmregister --s fsaverage \
  --mov $FSLDIR/etc/standard/avg152T1_brain.nii \
  --reg mni152.register.dat

It can be used like:

commit message:
In response to bug about 'Find Closest Vertex' command not working, did some work on the surface stuff.

- Found that Surf_ConvertVertexToVoxel and Surf_ConverVoxelToSurfaceSpace, which should be kinda opposites, were not. The former is used in surface draw list generation so it was tested, but the latter is used in the Find Closest Vertex stuff, and was causing the problem. In tkmedit.c, when Surf_New was called and the client transformation was passed it, it was being directly manipulated so the BtoRAS transform was not the inverse of RAStoB. So in tkmedit.c, I commented out that code. Then, while Surf_ConvertVertexToVoxel was using Trns_ConvertBRAStoB, Surf_ConverVoxelToSurfaceSpace was using Trns_ConvertAtoB, so I changed that to Trns_ConvertBtoRAS. So this seems to work now.

- The FindNearestSurfaceVertex functions were still calling the {MWin,DspA}_{Un}AdjustSurfaceDrawPoint functions. Since (I think) these are unnecessary now, I commented out the calls. We should probably just delete those {Un}Adjust functions, because they're not being used at all now.

Also I added keyboard shortcuts for the Find Nearest stuff.

commit message:
Creates a segmentation that can then be used with the geometric transfer matrix
for performing PET partial volume correction. It will create a segmentation of
the head (approximate extra-cerebral CSF, approximate skull, and the rest of
the head) using the xcerebralseg script. The WM can be subsegmented into lobes
with --subsegwm. Hypointensities can be kept with --keep-hypo. The corpus
callosum can be kept with --keep-cc. If these segments are not "kept" then
they are relabelled as WM. The upsampling factor (USF) controls the resolution
of the segmentation; this make a difference for cortical segmentations. Higher
resolution is more accurate but takes up more disk space and will require
more computations later on.

Fixing possible infinite recursion in trc/blood.cxx.

FindCenterStreamline function (in trc/blood.cxx) calls itself with different checking options set to true or false in certain cases. The base case (else branch on line 2429) potentially calls itself to infinity if it happens that hdmin's value is not changed from numeric_limits<double>::infinity(). I presume this has to do with some characteristic of a streamline being unsatisfactory. In any case, FindCenterStreamline should not call itself again if all the check variables are already set to false.

COMP: New cmake version (>=3.9) and new gcc compilers

New gcc compilers and clang compilers default to
more modern language standards.  The default
ubuntu 18.04 compiler default to CXX14 language
dialect by default.  In order to build freesurfer
against the explicitly specified CXX11 standard,
one should also build the external itk and vtk packages
against the CXX11 standard.

ITK has an explicit check that identifies when
ITK is built against C++14 and freesurfer is attempted
to build with C++11.

commit message:
centos9/gcc11, ITK5/VTK8 upgrade
  For filter multi-threading, a new signature has been introduced: void DynamicThreadedGenerateData( const OutputRegionType& threadRegion ).
  By default, this new signature is invoked instead of the classic void ThreadedGenerateData( const OutputRegionType& threadRegion, ThreadIdType threadId ).
  To temporarily obtain the old behavior (classic signature invoked by default), set ITKV4_COMPATIBILITY to ON in ITK's CMake configuration.
  To permanently have your filter use the classic threading model, invoke this->DynamicMultiThreadingOff(); in the filter constructor.

  invoke 'this->DynamicMultiThreadingOff();' in the following likelihoodImageFilters to use the clasic signature ThreadedGenerateData():
  kvlGMMLikelihoodImageFilter, kvlDSWbetaMMLikelihoodImageFilter, kvlFrobMMLikelihoodImageFilter, and kvlWMMLikelihoodImageFilter.

commit message:
This LTA maps between the 1mm, 256^3 RB_all_2008-03-26.mgh as created with

mri_convert $FREESURFER_HOME/average/RB_all_2008-03-26.gca RB_all_2008-03-26.mgh --conform

and MNI152_T1_2mm.nii.gz, the 2mm MNI152 space. This file was created
by first running recon-all with RB_all_2008-03-26.mgh as input. Then
mni152reg --s RB_all_2008-03-26 was run and the output converted to
LTA.

This LTA can be used something like

mri_vol2vol --gcam orig.mgz 0
 $SUBJECTS_DIR/subject/mri/transforms/talairach.m3z
 $FREESURFER_HOME/average/RB_all_2008-03-26.mni152.2mm.lta 0 0 out.mgh

tkregister2 --mov out.mgh --targ RB_all_2008-03-26.gca  --regheader --reg deleteme.dat

commit message:
This is an atlas that includes sulcal CSF, skull/bone, head tissue,
and air cavities insdie the head as well as pons and vermis.  It was
generated from 76 subjects from the IXI data set
http://www.brain-development.org (see below for demographics).

The extra cerebral labels were generated by first analyzing the T1s in
SPM "NewSeg" using the spmseg script. NewSeg creates segmentations
that include sulcal CSF, bone, and air. This seg was modified by
replacing the brain voxels with those from the aseg.

The vermis segmentation was complicated. The Buckner 40 was analyzed
in Suit to generate a vermis segmentation. This was then used to train
a gca. This gca was applied to the IXI data. It was then included
in the extra cerebral segmentation above.

The pons segmentation was performed by first hand labeling pons on the
MNI152. This was mapped to each IXI subject through a linear transform
and intersected with the brainstem label.

These segmentations where then used to train the atlas.

commit message:
Samples spmhrf at the given times.  fast_spmhrf will try
  to do some normalization, which changes the shape/amplitude when
  sampled over different times.  This works by sampling the HRF at a
  very fine resolution (1ms), then finding the values at tsamples in
  the oversampled HRF. The HRF is scaled such that the
  *oversampled* HRF is 1.0. The max of the returned hrf may or may
  not be 1.0 depending upon how close one of the tsamples falls
  to where the max is.

  If nderiv is > 0, then the gradient of the hires HRF is computed
  nderiv times then sampled at tsample. The 1ms sample time is
  factored in when compuding the gradient: hrf0 = gradient(hrf0,dt);

  tsamples can be a matrix.

commit message:
Modified the way the area of a vertex is computed. It used to be
computed by summing the neighboring triangles and dividing by 2, but
this is incorrect. It should be divided by 3. This bug was fixed in
version 1.306 and 1.307 in Nov of 2004, but the change was
inadvertently deleted within days. This does not have an effect on the
areas computed by mris_anatomical_stats because that program computes
the vertex area on its own, and it uses the correct formula. This does
affect the other stats from that program, namely the MeanCurv,
GausCurv, FoldInd, and CurvInd. This change also affects the output of
mri_surfcluster. It may also affect many other things because the
vertex area is used in a lot of places. Some of the other programs
affected might be: mris_compute_overlap, label_area.

commit message:
implement NIFTI_INTENT_DISPVECT io in niiRead()/niiWrite()
  - nifti file with intent code NIFTI_INTENT_DISPVECT has shape [5, c, r, s, 1, 3], and displacement field vector is in RAS space.
  - niiRead() handles up to 5 dimensions. The 5th dimensions are read as extra frames in MRI.
  - niiRead():  set intent=MGZ_INTENT_WARPMAP for nifti with intent code NIFTI_INTENT_DISPVECT
    niiWrite(): output warp (intent=MGZ_INTENT_WARPMAP) as nifti with intent code NIFTI_INTENT_DISPVECT

  * todo: In niiWrite(), the displacement field vector needs to converted to DISP_RAS before output

must have cerebellum segmented into cortex and WM. The output will
have cortex, core WM, and gyral WM.  The core WM will have IDs 7 and
46 (for left and right) and a gyral segmentation (690 and 691). None
of the other segmentations, including cerebellar GM, will be affected.

commit message:
% The purpose of this matlab script is to create the
% mni305.cor.subfov1.mgz and mni305.cor.subfov2.mgz volumes.  These
% are the same data as found in mni305.cor.mgz, but the field-of-view
% is much smaller and only covers the brain. The purpose of this is to
% reduce the amount of space needed to store the data. This is
% especially important when doing group functional analysis where
% there might be many subjects combined. In one subfov (subfov1), the
% voxel size is 1mm isotropic, 147 x 147 x 184. In the other (yep,
% subfov2), its 2mm isotropic,  74 x 74 x 92. These volumes are in
% register with mni305.cor.mgz in that the share the same RAS
% space, ie, you can run:
%   tkregister2 --targ mni305.cor.mgz --mov mni305.cor.subfov1.mgz \
%        --regheader --reg /tmp/reg
% And the volumes will be in register.

commit message:
Expanded 'mris_curvature_stats' to various surface integrals on the
following principle curvature functions:

	BE:	"Bending Energy" 	= k1^2 + k2^2
	SI:	"Shape Index"		= atan((k1+k2)/(k2-k1)
	C:	"Curvedness"		= sqrt(0.5*(k1^2+k2^2)
	S:	"Sharpness"		= (k1 - k2)^2

Surface integrals are all area normalized, and the following
integrals are computed:

	"Natural" : 	No change to vertex curvature
	"Rectified" :	fabs(vertex->curv)
	"Positive":	vertex->curv >= 0
	"Negative":	vertex->curv < 0

In the case of "positive" and "negative", only those parts of
the surface that correspond to the constraint are considered
in the integral.

Additionally, 'mris_curvature_stats' will output FreeSurfer
curvature files of the above "BE", "SI", "C", and "S" functions:

	$SUBJ/surf/<hemi>.<surface>.BE|SI|C|S.crv

author: Henry Tregidgo <h.tregidgo@ucl.ac.uk>
commit message:
bf: Fix tensorflow macos arm compatability

Fixes issues with some of the tensorflow based tools when running on an
arm based macos machine (M1, M2, M3 chipset). The two main issues are:

	1. a check for np.float128 which isn't a supported datatype on
	   this chipset
	2. an error in the shape of tensors provided to batch-
	   normalisation layers

Issue 1 can be fixed by removing the check as it's not likely to be
necessary in most cases.

Issue 2 arrises as there are two implementations of batch norm in
keras (fused/unfused). Tensors of rank 5 are not supported in the
faster fused version, so a check is performed based on the input shape
and the correct version should be selected. For some reason this check
isn't working on the macOS arm chipsets (possibly a tensorflow-metal or
keras version issue) and this causes the shape mismatch at inference.

Checking behaviour on an Ubuntu installation the batch norm does seem to
default to the non-fused version so explicitly setting fused=False at
network construction should avoid the issue altogether.

commit message:
T2/FLAIR Pial: added treatment for longitudinal processing
a) if -t2pial is passed in long, it will either use the input from -T2 or if not available will use the T2/FLAIR from the cross automatically
b) if the T2/FLAIR was used in cross it will concatenate the ltas to map the T2raw to the longitudinal space
c) if no lta is available from cross it will compute it with bbregister

Also changed the cross sectional stream, it now uses the T2raw or FLAIRraw and registers it directly to the subject instead of creating an intermediate conformed volume. Also allows using the cubic interpolation now.

commit message:
The purpose of this program is to create a volume with a smaller field
of view by creating a bounding box small enough to encompass a
mask. The bounding box can be expanded by npad number of voxels. Other
volumes that are the same size as the input mask can be reduced to the
bounding box. If a registration file for the input mask is passed,
then a new registration file is created that can be applied to the new
field of view.

FS-FAST routine to mask out regions from a contrast that are not
in the brain. You can specify multiple contrasts and multiple maps
inside a contrast (all maps must exist inside all contrasts).

The routine will use the brain mask as found in bold/masks. This
can be created with mkbrainmask-sess. All voxels outside of this
region will be set to 0. The resulting map will be called map-brain
and can be accessed with all the commands that would normally be
used to viewed maps (eg, sliceview, tkmedit, etc).

commit message:
Warpfield
  1. Warpfield::read() - check if given mgz is a warp file
  2. add description of mgz warp format
     The warp file follows mgz format with these tags:
       TAG_GCAMORPH_GEOM   followed by gcamorph image (source) geom and gcamorph atlas (target) geom
       TAG_WARPFIELD_DTFMT followed by one of these - WARPFIELD_DTFMT_ABS_CRS|WARPFIELD_DTFMT_DISP_CRS|WARPFIELD_DTFMT_ABS_RAS|WARPFIELD_DTFMT_DISP_RAS

     The 3-D data array is indexed by atlas crs.
     Here are the values for the 4 data formats supported:
       WARPFIELD_DTFMT_ABS_CRS   - crs coordinates in image space
       WARPFIELD_DTFMT_DISP_CRS  - displacement crs, delta = image_crs - atlas_crs
       WARPFIELD_DTFMT_ABS_RAS   - ras coordinates in image space
       WARPFIELD_DTFMT_DISP_RAS  - displacement ras, delta = image_ras - atlas_ras

commit message:
gcamorph.cpp/tags.cpp - m3z TAG read
  There are two data formats for TAG output:
    a) "tagid data-length data"
    b) "tagid data" (the data length is fixed and known to freesurfer).

  TAG_GCAMORPH_GEOM/TAG_GCAMORPH_TYPE/TAG_GCAMORPH_LABELS are in format (b).
  TAG_MGH_XFORM is used in both mgz and m3z, but in different format.
  It is format (a) in mgz, and format (b) in m3z.
  Optional parameter is added to znzTAGreadStart() to handle the situation.

  Change __m3zRead() to read TAGs using znzTAGreadStart() instead of znzreadIntEx().
  This makes it consistent with TAG read in mgz file.
  It also makes it possible to handle TAGs in format (a), and skip the TAGs and data if needed.

output mgz TAGs as nifti1 header extension
  1. introduce end of extension data tag TAG_END_NIIHDREXTENSION
  2. write TAG_END_NIIHDREXTENSION at the end of extension data to avoid the data to be truncated:
       TAG_END_NIIHDREXTENSION (-1)  data-length (1) '*'

  note: If the extension data has trailing null characters or zeros at the end,
        nibabel.nifti1.Nifti1Extension.get_content() will truncate the data.
        See https://github.com/nipy/nibabel/blob/master/nibabel/nifti1.py#L629C1-L630C1,

SUMMARY

Converts a label or a set of labels into a volume. For a single lable,
the volume will be binary: 1 where the label is and 0 where it is not.
For multiple labels, the volume will be 0 where no labels were found
otherwise the value will the the label number. For a voxel to be
declared part of a label, it must have enough hits in the voxel and
it must have more hits than any other label.

places.

commit message:
This is a GCA used to compute the aseg. It was trained from the manual
labels in the buckner39 using the mni305-based talairach.xfm as the
affine transform. The purpose is so that mri_em_register does not need
to be run, mri_ca_register can just use the talairach.xfm (converted
to lta); this saves 15-20 min.  In jack-knifed tests using the
bucker39, the dice performance was nearly identical to that when
mri_em_register was used instead.

setenv SUBJECTS_DIR /autofs/cluster/freesurfer/subjects/atlases/fsv6.aseg_atlas
cd /autofs/cluster/freesurfer/subjects/atlases/fsv6.aseg_atlas
gcatrain --g dev.gca.seg_edited10.talxfm305 --f fsv6.aseg.train.slist.txt --niters 2 --nthreads 2 --seg seg_edited10.mgz --init v6.990104_vc700 talairach.xfm.lta --no-emreg

T2/FLAIR Pial: added treatment for longitudinal processing
a) if -t2pial is passed in long, it will either use the input from -T2 or if not
 available will use the T2/FLAIR from the cross automatically
b) if the T2/FLAIR was used in cross it will concatenate the ltas to map the T2raw to the longitudinal space
c) if no lta is available from cross it will compute it with bbregister

Also changed the cross sectional stream, it now uses the T2raw or FLAIRraw and r
egisters it directly to the subject instead of creating an intermediate conforme
d volume. Also allows using the cubic interpolation now.

% [tpr tnc] = fast_glmpower(beta,X,rvar,C,alpha,nsides)
%
% Computes the power (ie, true positive rate) of a hypothetical
% GLM analysis. NOTE: requires statistics toolbox.
%
% beta - vector of hypothetical regression coefficients
% X - deisgn matrix (dof = size(X,1) - size(X,2))
% rvar - hypothetical variance (scalar)
% C - contrast matrix (only one row allowed)
% alpha - Type I Error Rate (can be a vector)
% nsides - 1 for one-sided t test, or 2 for two-sided t test
%   default is one-sided.
%
% tpr = 1 - Type II Error Rate (vector same length as alpha)
% tnc = noncentrality parameter
%
% See also: fast_glmfitw, fast_fratiow, FTest.

annot was created called ?h.labels.DKT31.manual.2.annot that had these
removed.

The following command was used:

train-gcs-atlas --src labels.DKT31.manual.2 \
  --f mindboggle101_list.txt --rh  \
  --reg sphere.folding.atlas.acfb40.noaparc.i12.2016-08-02.reg \
  --o gcs/rh.DKTaparc.atlas.acfb40.noaparc.i12.2020-05-13.gcs

?h.sphere.folding.atlas.acfb40.noaparc.i12.2016-08-02.reg is the
registration to the V6 folding atlas (see reg-to-v6). However, this
folding atlas is also used in V7, so it is ok to create aparc atlases
with it for V7.

commit message:
Change a lot more modifies of xyz to use MRISsetXYZ

        Free the VERTEX::dist in many more places where the dist is invalid, to verify it is being recomputed with the new xyz values

        Use MRISexportXYZ rather than VERTEX::tdxyz in some cases to reduce usage of the tdxyz and get better memory traffic performance

        Add base.h copeWithLogicProblem that allows reporting and optional fixing of possible logic problems in the code

        Move origxyz after xyz in the VERTEX because xyz is the input and origxyz is the output

        Start keeping track of the dist_orig_nsize because changing dist_nsize did not always recompute the corresponding dist_orig values

        Replace calls to the badly misnamed MRIScomputeGeometricProperties with the existing MRIS_facesAtVertices_reorder, because that is what it does

        Passed __FILE__ and __LINE__ into MRISsetXYZ to allow for better warning messages

        Added and used MRISblendXYZandTXYZ   (mris, ...) rather than having multiple copies of the operation   (xyz = a * xyz + b * txyz)

        Added and used MRISscaleThenTranslate(mris, ...) rather than having multiple copies of the operation   (x = ax * x + bx), (y = ay * y + by), ...

        Use mrisComputeSurfaceDimensions rather than having multiple copies of the operation

        Logic errors being flagged
            mris_sphere/mris_sphere.c main()
                is not copying the xyz into the origxyz
                hence is later using zeroes rather than the correct values
            utils/mrisurf_integrate.c MRISinflateBrain()
                is not copying the xyz into the origxyz
                hence is later using zeroes rather than the correct values

        Add a primitive restart capability to recon-all
            so that the initial expensive mri section can be skipped when working on mris code

        Share the code for mrisComputeVertexDistance and mrisComputeOriginalVertexDistance
            so that they use the exact same definition of distance - the OriginalVertex version had not been updated when the Vertex version was sped up

        Speed up the deallocation and reallocation dist and dist_orig so it is cheap to have the dist and dist_orig fields NULL when the values are invalid

        Added mrisComputeOriginalVertexDistancesIfNecessary which will compute the dist_orig if they are not already computed
            This is useful for correctly logic errors where some paths had not computed the dist_orig and other paths might have

        Added to MRIS_facesAtVertices_reorder to fill in the topology correctly

        Renamed MRIScomputeNormals MRIScomputeNormalsPerturbingXYZ because the former does not capture the idea that the xyz might be changed by this call

commit message:
Implements a masked smoothing in which the input (vsm) is unchanged in
voxels that have a non-zero value. In voxels with a zero value, the
value is replaced with vsm smoothed by the given amount. This will
likely only change the voxels that are near the edge of the non-zero
voxels. This is a simple way to extrapolate the non-zero voxels beyond
their range. This works well for a B0 distortion correction voxel
shift map (vsm), but it can be applied to other maps.

commit message:
Undo AutoScale Functor in dcm2niix conversion
  At the Martinos scanners, AutoScale functor scales data before saving them to DICOM.
  The scale factor is saved in DICOM tag (0020, 4000). Dcm2niix retrieves (0020, 4000) as image comments,
  and saves it in nifti header field aux_file. The string format is `Scale Factor: %f`.

  The scale factors are saved in dcm2niix - nii_dicom_batch.cpp::saveDcm2NiiCore().
  In niiReadFromMriFsStruct(), we use the scale factors to undo the scaling applied by AutoScale functor.
  The volume is created with data type MRI_FLOAT if we need to undo the scaling.

  Similar logic is also implemented in DICOMRead.cpp::sdcmLoadVolumeAutoScale() when not converting with dcm2niix.

  - DICOMRead3()
    signature change: 'convert' is false by default, add optional parameter std::vector<std::vector<float>> **
  - packages/dcm2niix
    1. save autoscale factors for each slice
    2. add interface to retrieve the autoscale factors
    * the changes haven't been tested with ENHANCED DICOM format.
      Autoscale has 2 modes of operation: Scale by slice and Scale by volume.
      Not sure the changes will work in 'Scale by slice' mode for ENHANCED DICOM.

Aligns and averages two or more volumes. Uses the FSL flirt program.
Actually calls fsl_rigid_register which calls flirt. See
fsl_rigid_register -help. This should basically do the same thing
as mri_motion_correct and mri_motion_correct2. One difference is
that mri_motion_correct.fsl forces the input data to be float
when converting to ANALYZE, and so the final output is is also float.
mri_motion_correct2 keeps the native precision.

commit message:
MRISurfOverlay class
  This class implements methods to read/write Freesurfer overlay files.
    The following file formats are supported:
      shape measurements (.curv, .sulc, .area, .thickness), .mgh (stats), .gii
      (MRI_CURV_FILE, MRI_MGH_FILE, GIFTI_FILE).
      MRI_CURV_FILE is the new CURV format with MAGICNO. = 16777215.

    Overlay files can also be in MRIS_ASCII_FILE, MRIS_VTK_FILE, and old CURV formats.
    These formats are still handled by MRISreadCurvatureFile()/MRISwriteCurvature().

  The overlay data has 1D morphometry data (vertex-wise measures) or other per-vertex information.
  The data is read into MRI representation in this class.

commit message:
Added a 'mod' function:

        The 'mod' operation is performed by a call to the C-function, fmod(),
        and accepts either integer or floats -- in fact, ints are converted
        to floats for this operation.  Output sign convention and 0 handling
        follows that of fmod():

        fmod ( ±0, y )   returns ±0 for y not zero.
        fmod ( x, y )    returns a NaN and raises the invalid floating-point
                         exception for x infinite or y zero.
        fmod ( x, ±inf ) returns x for x not infinite.

This behaviour is analogous to the MatLAB rem(...) function.

fem_elastic/gems - centos9/gcc11, ITK5 upgrade
  Errors similar to error: conversion from 'int' to 'typename InterpolatorType::Pointer' are a result of further type safety for dealing with pointers.
  Enhancements in nullptr behavior in ITKv5 provide more clear type checking and respect the nullptr identifier.
  The 'long 0' value known as NULL causes an ambiguity for overload compilations of the ITKv5 smartpointers.
  To be backwards compatible with pre C++11 compilers use the ITK_NULLPTR designation, otherwise replace NULL and 0 initialization of itk::SmartPointer with nullptr.

commit message:
Computes the partial correlation coefficient (PCC) for each contrast
in the output dir of mri_glmfit. It also computes a z-score map. The
z is "two-sided" meaning that if it is converted back to a p, it
must be done with a two-sized computation to get the original
p-value. This matches how selxavg3 creates z-scores (and I think FSL
too).  The output will be two files called pcc.ext and z.ext where
ext is the file format extension found in the glmdir folder.

Added the following functionality:

	ACTION  INPUTS OUTPUTS	                EFFECT
     MATHEMATICAL
	  sqd	   2	  1     <outputFile> = (<file1> - <file2>)^2
	  sqr	   1      1	<outputFile> = <file1> * <file1>
	  sqrt	   1      1     <outputFile> = sqrt(<file1>)

      STATISTICAL
	  sum	   1      0	print the sum across all values of <file1>
	  prod	   1      0     print the inner product across <file1>

To determine the sum squared different between F1.mgz and F2.mgz:

$>mris_calc -o F1-F2.sqd.mgz F1.mgz sqd F2.mgz
$>mris_calc F1-F2.sqd.mgz sum

author: Kevin Teich <kteich@nmr.mgh.harvard.edu>
commit message:
Rewritten to solve problems between multiple indexing schemes used in
this code, between assuming that tables had no empty or skipped
fields. New code allows NULL or empty entries, but clients must be
careful that they are thinking of 'structure indecies' in the right
way.

- Change the color table so that we don't have to convert structure to
index; it is costly as it involves a O(n) search through the
table. The table in memory will just have empty entries for the
skipped structures. However, it means that our color tables become
crazy long when we skip a lot of entries (as in the
FreeSurferColorLUT.txt which goes up to 5000 entries), so we waste a
lot of memory. (All my code is doing this internally already, tho, as
it's too slow to do it the CTAB way; this is why CTAB isn't breaking
tkmedit and scuba right now.)

- Change all the CTAB functions so they only use 'index', which means
both 0-based table index as well as structure number.

- Change the binary CTAB format so that it writes a negative version
number first. Then, when we read the first int from the binary stream,
we see if it's < 0, and if so, use the new version 2 format.

- The version 2 format of the binary CTAB code will write structure
numbers so we our binary format is in line with the ASCII file format.

curvature file (?h.{curv.sulc}) and the surface (often ?h.smoothwm).

defects.

In such a case if incompatibilities are detected, 'mris_curvature_stats'
will skip any processing of the curvature file. If a Gaussian analysis
has been specified, 'mris_curvature_stats' will proceed with this
Gaussian analysis.

from a mask of the brain (brain.mgz). This will more-or-less give a

dura, skull, eyes, vessels). The original purpose of this program was
create regressors for fMRI using extra-cerebral CSF.

% mri = MRIread(fspec,headeronly)
%
% Reads in a volume based on the fspec. fspec can be:
%  1. MGH file. Eg, f.mgh or f.mgz
%  2. BVolume Stem. Eg, f for f_000.bshort or f_000.bfloat
%
% Creates a structure similar to the FreeSurfer MRI struct
% defined in mri.h. Times are in ms and angles are in radians.
% The vox2ras0 matrix is the matrix that converts a 0-based
% column, row, and slice to XYZ. vox2ras1 is the same with
% 1-based indices. The volume is rows, cols, slices frames,
% but the vox2ras expects col, row, slice.
%
% If headeronly=1, then the pixel data is not read in.

commit message:
% [segname, segindex, segstats] = load_segstats(segstatsfile,<subject>)
%
% Loads data from stats file produced by mri_segstats. This
% includes the aseg.stats produced by recon-all.
%
% segstatsfile - path to seg stats file
% subject - optional. Looks for segstatsfile relative to
%    SUBJECTS_DIR/subject/stats. If segstatsfile is empty,
%    then loads SUBJECTS_DIR/subject/stats/aseg.stats
%
%  segname is a list of the segmentation names
%    (col 5 from aseg.stats file)
%  segindex is the index of each segmentation
%  segstats are the stats for each index. Each col is a stat:
%    1. number of voxels
%    2. volume of voxels (mm^3) -- same as number but scaled by voxvol
%    3. mean intensity over space
%    4. std intensity over space
%    5. min intensity over space
%    6. max intensity over space
%    7. range intensity over space
%
% The intensities are from whatever was passed as the --in volume
% to mri_segstats. For aseg.stats, this is the norm.mgz volume.
%
% Any line that begins with a '#' is ignored.
%
% Examples:
% [segname segindex segstats] = load_segstats(segstatsfile);
% [segname segindex segstats] = load_segstats(segstatsfile,'bert');
% [segname segindex segstats] = load_segstats([],'bert');

author: Rudolph Pienaar <rudolph@nmr.mgh.harvard.edu>
commit message:
Added more robust checking for whether inputs are valid files
or float arguments.

'mris_calc' was susceptible to being fooled if input file arg spec
started with a sequence of numeric chars. The test for conversion
of name to numeric failed, and in the process corrupted the file
arg, resulting in 'mris_calc' not being able to find the file
either.

This now more robustly handled by 'mris_calc' checking if input
arg is a valid file using stat(...) -- if file does not exist,
'mris_calc' then attempts to convert to float. Float conversion
is only considered valid if no spurious characters remain at
end of conversion string. If spurious characters remain (as in
a strtof conversion of, for e.g., '2.145test' then the string
is assumed to refer to a file, which will then fail.

If a filespec is masked by a file on the filesystem with the same
name, then the file is interpreted and NOT the float conversion.
For example, if you have a file called '100' which a valid mgz
volume, and run 'mris_calc somefile.mgz mul 100', the the file
'100' will be accessed and not considered to mean the number
100.

by a subject-specific anatomical ROI, and, possibly, a
subject-specific functional ROI. The summary table (-o) is a simple
text file that has a row for each session followed by the mean
contrast (ces) inside the boundaries of the ROI.

commit message:
Added several additional 'operators':


      RELATIONAL
          lt       2      1     <outputFile> = <file1> <  <file2>
          lte      2      1     <outputFile> = <file1> <= <file2>
          gt       2      1     <outputFile> = <file1> >  <file2>
          gte      2      1     <outputFile> = <file1> >= <file2>
          upl      2      1     <outputFile> = <file1> upperlimit <file2>
          lrl      2      1     <outputFile> = <file1> lowerlimit <file2>

        LOGICAL
          and      2      1     <outputFile> = <file1> && <file2>
           or      2      1     <outputFile> = <file1> || <file2>
         andbw     2      1     <outputFile> = (int)<file1> & (int)<file2>
          orbw     2      1     <outputFile> = (int)<file1> | (int)<file2>
         masked    2      1     <outputFile> = <file1> maskedby <file2>


See 'mris_calc -u' for more details.

Refactored some internals: use enumerated date type for tracking operations
instead of relying on cumbersome string comparisons (strcmp).

Updated help.txt accordingly.

These are created by mksubfov.m. Here's the doc for that program.

% The purpose of this matlab script is to create the
% mni305.cor.subfov1.mgz and mni305.cor.subfov2.mgz volumes.  These
% are the same data as found in mni305.cor.mgz, but the field-of-view
% is much smaller and only covers the brain. The purpose of this is to
% reduce the amount of space needed to store the data. This is
% especially important when doing group functional analysis where
% there might be many subjects combined. In one subfov (subfov1), the
% voxel size is 1mm isotropic, 151 x 151 x 186. In the other (yep,
% subfov2), its 2mm isotropic,  76 x 76 x 93. These volumes are in
% register with mni305.cor.mgz in that the share the same RAS
% space, ie, you can run:
%   tkregister2 --targ mni305.cor.mgz --mov mni305.cor.subfov1.mgz \
%        --regheader --reg /tmp/reg
% And the volumes will be in register.
%
% After these files are created by this program, run the following:
%   mri_convert mni305.cor.subfov1.mgz mni305.cor.subfov1.mgz --odt uchar
%   mri_convert mni305.cor.subfov2.mgz mni305.cor.subfov2.mgz --odt uchar
% This just reduces the size by a factor of 4.

commit message:
fscalc.fsl - a freesurfer wrapper around fslmaths

This is a utility that extends fslmaths so that any format that can
be read/written by freesurfer can be used. It operates in the same
way as fslmaths, just use the same command line flags and arguments
with the exception that the input file formats can be anything that
freesurfer reads, and the output file format can be anything that
freesurfer writes. Note that volume-encoded surface files will still
fail due to nifti dimension incompatibility. See fslmaths for more
info.

Computes the in-brain mean value of the given input volume.
The result is stored in instem.meanval unless otherwise
specified.

By default, "In-brain" is defined by thresholding the input volume
at .75 of its grand mean and then dilating by 1 voxel. If a mask is
specified, then the voxels in the mask define in-brian.

Autodetects format from the input stem.

Runs matlab.

Added ability for the user to require that the build stamp be
consitent from one recon-all invokation to the next. To do this,
define:

setenv REQUIRE_FS_MATCH 1

If it is not defined or set to 0, then a match is not required. If
it is defined and 1, then checks $FREESURFER_HOME/build-stamp.txt
against that in the subject's scripts dir. If they are not the
same, then it exits immediately with an error.

mris_convert
  1. MRISread(), MRISreadPatch(), MRISreadPatchNoRemove() - take an optional argument to decide whether to convert surface x,y,z to tkregister space. The default is true.
  2. mris_convert - respect surface space when reading one of the following: in file (patch file when -p is specified), second in file to be combined, --to-surf <surface-coord-file>
  3. MRIScopyCoords() - also copy mris->useRealRAS, and volgeom if it is valid. The function is used in mris_convert and mris_flatten.
  4. MRISunion()  - add checks for volgeom/space, make sure they are the same in both surface.  The function is only used in mris_convert.

vglrun allows some graphical applications to run faster when on remote desktops
such as NoMachine. There are several conditions that must be met before
vglrun will be used:
  1. the environment variable FS_ALLOW_VGLRUN but be set to non-zero
  2. vglrun must exist in the path or in /usr/pubsw/bin/vglrun
  3. the shell should not be local (ie, must be a remote shell),
     thought it might not hurt to use vglrun if it is local

commit message:
Computes the average of a volume inside a given segment of a
segmentation resampling the input volume to the segmentation
space. The output can be a text file or a volume format (eg, .mgh,
.nii). If the volume has multiple time points, then the output will
have multiple time points. If a segmentation id is not supplied, then
1 is assumed.  By default, the binarized segmentation is reduced in
size to a bounding box that covers the segmentation. This can be much
more computationally efficient, especially when the input has many
time points. This is basically a frontend for mri_segstats with the
difference being that mri_segstats requires that the input volume and
segmentation must be in the same space. mri_segstats will report on
each segmentation and reduce certain segmentations into a single
segmentation.

commit message:
bf: large FOV memory bad alloc

Some volumes default to an in plane field of view of 256 by 256 voxels
even when their voxel sizes are larger than 1mm in plane. This can
result in much larger tensors when pre-upsampling to 1mm isotropic,
which in turn can cause unhandled memory allocation issues on smaller
machines.

The fix here it to include an --autocrop option which detects non-
background voxels and crops to a bounding box. Here non-background is
defined as voxel intensity greater than 0 after the re-normalisation
and intensity clipping steps. Testing on ADNI led to a greater than
fourfold reduction in tensor size.

err = convert_fieldsign(infname,outfname)

  Loads a field sign (infname) as saved by the void write_fieldsign()
  in tksurfer and saves in the given output format. This allows the
  field sign map to be loaded as an overlay in tksurfer. This can
  also be used to convert a field sign mask.

  Eg:
   In matlab:
     convert_fieldsign('fieldsign-lh','lh.fieldsign.mgh');
     convert_fieldsign('fieldsignmask-lh','lh.fieldsignmask.mgh');
   In the unix shell:
     mri_mask lh.fieldsign.mgh lh.fieldsignmask.mgh lh.fieldsign-masked.mgh
     tksurfer subjectname lh inflated \
       -overlay lh.fieldsign-masked.mgh -fthresh 0.5

Added 'noSync' command to 'dsh'. This turns OFF the timed pulsing between
the shell 'dsh' and the back-end 'mris_pmake' process. Useful if the
'mris_pmake' is running an embedded/compiled script and does not return
to its main event loop for some time. While the compiled script is running
'dsh' would probably keep sending timed pulses to 'mris_pmake' in an effort
to get a 'Ready' string back. If a compiled script is running, no 'Ready'
will be returned until the script terminates.

% [csort rhosort zrhoabs] = fast_corsort(rho,Nps)
% rho is an NxN correlation matrix
% Nps is a list of number of inputs for each subject
%   sum(Nps) must equal N (the size of rho)
%   Eg, if there were 3 subjects each with 4 inputs, then
%      Nps = [4 4 4];
%   Eg, if the 2nd subject had 5 then
%      Nps = [4 5 4];
% csort will be Nmin by Ns, where Nmin = min(Nps) and Ns
%   is the number of subjects. Each row of csort represents
%   a "coherent component". The number in csort is the
%   subject component that belongs to that coherent component.
% rhosort - correlation values corresponding to the components
% zrhoabs - used for debugging.
%
% Eg:
%   y is component-by-space matrix
%   yn = fast_fnorm(y,2,1); % Normalize across space
%   rho = yn*yn'; % Cor Coeff across component

specify a full path, output files will be written relative to the current

directory structure

Behavior is unchanged if the FS_POSIX environment variable is not set.

commit message:
Added '--signedPrinciples' command line option. This affects how the
K1 and K2 principle curvatures are assigned when derived curvatures
are calculated.

In the original way, K1 and K2 are assigned the fabs(max) and fabs(min)
candidate principle solutions respectively.

This flag allows an alternate assignment where K1=max and K2=min.

The 'help.txt' is a text file containing the man page of
'mris_curvature_stats'. The 'makehelp.sh' simply appends
'\n' to each line of 'help.txt'. Thus, to edit the man page, make
changes to 'help.txt', and then run 'makehelp.sh' This will
create 'helpn.txt'. Simply embed the contents of 'helpn.txt'
into the 'print_help(void)' function body.

commit message:
Transferred discrete principle curvature functions to mris.[ch]

o Traditionally, the principle curvatures are calculated with:

	int MRIScomputeSecondFundamentalForm(MRI_SURFACE *mris) ;

o To use the new discrete-based code, use:

	short MRIScomputeSecondFundamentalFormDiscrete(MRIS* apmris);

Note that

int          MRIScomputeSecondFundamentalFormAtVertex(MRI_SURFACE *mris,
                                                      int vno,
                                                      int *vertices,
                                                      int vnum) ;
int          MRIScomputeSecondFundamentalFormThresholded(MRI_SURFACE *mris,
                                                         double thresh) ;

still use the traditional (i.e. non-discrete) methods.


-=R

commit message:
bf: more managed xyz and dist 2 (#604)

*         Change a lot more modifies of xyz to use MRISsetXYZ

        Free the VERTEX::dist in many more places where the dist is invalid, to verify it is being recomputed with the new xyz values

        Use MRISexportXYZ rather than VERTEX::tdxyz in some cases to reduce usage of the tdxyz and get better memory traffic performance

        Add base.h copeWithLogicProblem that allows reporting and optional fixing of possible logic problems in the code

        Move origxyz after xyz in the VERTEX because xyz is the input and origxyz is the output

        Start keeping track of the dist_orig_nsize because changing dist_nsize did not always recompute the corresponding dist_orig values

        Replace calls to the badly misnamed MRIScomputeGeometricProperties with the existing MRIS_facesAtVertices_reorder, because that is what it does

        Passed __FILE__ and __LINE__ into MRISsetXYZ to allow for better warning messages

        Added and used MRISblendXYZandTXYZ   (mris, ...) rather than having multiple copies of the operation   (xyz = a * xyz + b * txyz)

        Added and used MRISscaleThenTranslate(mris, ...) rather than having multiple copies of the operation   (x = ax * x + bx), (y = ay * y + by), ...

        Use mrisComputeSurfaceDimensions rather than having multiple copies of the operation

        Logic errors being flagged
            mris_sphere/mris_sphere.c main()
                is not copying the xyz into the origxyz
                hence is later using zeroes rather than the correct values
            utils/mrisurf_integrate.c MRISinflateBrain()
                is not copying the xyz into the origxyz
                hence is later using zeroes rather than the correct values

        Add a primitive restart capability to recon-all
            so that the initial expensive mri section can be skipped when working on mris code

        Share the code for mrisComputeVertexDistance and mrisComputeOriginalVertexDistance
            so that they use the exact same definition of distance - the OriginalVertex version had not been updated when the Vertex version was sped up

        Speed up the deallocation and reallocation dist and dist_orig so it is cheap to have the dist and dist_orig fields NULL when the values are invalid

        Added mrisComputeOriginalVertexDistancesIfNecessary which will compute the dist_orig if they are not already computed
            This is useful for correctly logic errors where some paths had not computed the dist_orig and other paths might have

        Added to MRIS_facesAtVertices_reorder to fill in the topology correctly

        Renamed MRIScomputeNormals MRIScomputeNormalsPerturbingXYZ because the former does not capture the idea that the xyz might be changed by this call

* Fix a crash when the logStatus called was trying to computeSSE when it had not computed dist

* Be quieter about the logic problems for now

* Be quieter, like before

* Start working towards correcting the calculation of dist and dist_orig

* Set origxyz and compute dist_orig before first iteration

* Flag but don't automatically fix more logic errors

* Be more consistent about maintaining MRIS::avg_nbrs and dist_orig

* Make a smaller step detecting the bugs

* Fix setting avg_nbrs and nsize

* Preserve the old behavior for avg_nbrs for now

* Start fixing the problems in quad writing and reading

* Add fixes for reading and writing QUAD files, and tidy up the new versions

* Select the new behaviour for MRISwrite and MRISreadOverAlloc - they now check whether triangles abut before merging into a quad, and cope with a quad with two or more equal vertices

* Turn off checks

SUMMARY

Front end for FSLs PRELUDE and FUGUE programs to correct for B0
distortion in functional EPI scans. The programs use a B0 fieldmap.
This is assumed to be two conventional GREs collected at two different
echo times (TEs). The field map should be acquired with the same
slice prescription, slice thickness, slice skip, and field-of-view
as the EPI. The field map can have a higher in-plane resolution.

% [sig gmn gmnvar t dof p] = fast_ffx(means,varmeans,dofs,X,C)
%
% Group-level fixed effects analysis
%   means    is nsamples-by-nvoxels
%   varmeans is nsamples-by-nvoxels
%   dof = sum(dofs) [if dofs is a scalar, then dof = nsamples*dofs]
%   X is nsamples-by-nX (if not spec or empty, then X = ones(nsamples,1))
%   C is J-by-nX (if not spec or empty, then C = eye(nX))
%
%   gamma    = inv(X'*X)*X'*means;  (J-by-nvox)
%   gammavar = inv(X'*X)*X'*diag(varmeans)*X*inv(X'*X); (J^2-by-nvox)
%   F = gamma'*inv(gammavar)*gamma/J; (1-by-nvox)
%   p = FTest(J, dof, F); (1-by-nvox)
%
% When X is the ones vector and C=1, then gives the same result as
% fast_ffx_osgm.

and air cavities insdie the head. It was generated from 76 subjects
from the IXI data set http://www.brain-development.org (see below for

include sulcal CSF, bone, and air. This seg was modified by replacing
the brain voxels with those from the aseg. These 79 segmentations
where then used to train this atlas.

commit message:
err = fast_svextreg(extreg,stem)

  Saves a matrix in a way that it can be used
  as an external regressor for FS-FAST.

  extreg is the nframes-by-nregressors matrix
  stem is the bfloat stem to save it in

  Eg,
    nframes = 100; % timepoints
    nreg    =   3; % number of regressors
    extreg  = randn(nframes,nreg);
    fast_svextreg(extreg,'mystem');

  This will create mystem_000.bfloat, mystem_000.hdr, and
  mystem.bhdr. When running mkanalysis-sess, use -extreg mystem.

This creates an average subcortical mask for the given inputs
subjects. For each subject, we first create a binary mask from the
aseg by removing the following structures:

Background 0
Cerebral Cortex 3 42
Cerebral White Matter 2 41
CC 251 252 253 254 255
Cerebellar White Matter 7 46
Ventricles 4 14 15 43 44 72 75 76 24
Choroid Plexus 31 63

This mask is then converted to "talairach" space (meaning, conformed
MNI305 like fsaverage) using the talairach.xfm.  All the subjects are
averaged together, so each voxel contains a number between 0 and 1,
with 1 indicating that it is highly likely that there is a subcortical
gray matter structure at that location.

The purpose of this is to create a mask for doing volume-based
fMRI analysis of subcortical structure (assuming that the
cortical analysis is going to be done on the surface).

This is a script that runs a comprehensive group analysis on both maps
and ROI results.  This script was originally designed to assist in the
testing of FreeSurfer output (in conjunction with groupstatsdiff), so
there are a lot of tests performed, more than one would normally do
for a typical study. However, it is possible to use this to do almost
all of your group analysis as it runs mris_preproc for the maps and
asegstats2table/aparcstats2table for the ROIs and then mri_glmfit for
both.

commit message:
bf: Fix tensorflow macos arm compatability (#1192)

* bf: Fix tensorflow macos arm compatability

Fixes issues with some of the tensorflow based tools when running on an
arm based macos machine (M1, M2, M3 chipset). The two main issues are:

	1. a check for np.float128 which isn't a supported datatype on
	   this chipset
	2. an error in the shape of tensors provided to batch-
	   normalisation layers

Issue 1 can be fixed by removing the check as it's not likely to be
necessary in most cases.

Issue 2 arrises as there are two implementations of batch norm in
keras (fused/unfused). Tensors of rank 5 are not supported in the
faster fused version, so a check is performed based on the input shape
and the correct version should be selected. For some reason this check
isn't working on the macOS arm chipsets (possibly a tensorflow-metal or
keras version issue) and this causes the shape mismatch at inference.

Checking behaviour on an Ubuntu installation the batch norm does seem to
default to the non-fused version so explicitly setting fused=False at
network construction should avoid the issue altogether.

* bf: fix macos m3 bug in easyreg

commit message:
In response to bug about 'Find Closest Vertex' command not working, did some work on the surface stuff.

- Found that Surf_ConvertVertexToVoxel and Surf_ConverVoxelToSurfaceSpace, which should be kinda opposites, were not. The former is used in surface draw list generation so it was tested, but the latter is used in the Find Closest Vertex stuff, and was causing the problem. In tkmedit.c, when Surf_New was called and the client transformation was passed it, it was being directly manipulated so the BtoRAS transform was not the inverse of RAStoB. So in tkmedit.c, I commented out that code. Then, while Surf_ConvertVertexToVoxel was using Trns_ConvertBRAStoB, Surf_ConverVoxelToSurfaceSpace was using Trns_ConvertAtoB, so I changed that to Trns_ConvertBtoRAS. So this seems to work now.

- The FindNearestSurfaceVertex functions were still calling the {MWin,DspA}_{Un}AdjustSurfaceDrawPoint functions. Since (I think) these are unnecessary now, I commented out the calls. We should probably just delete those {Un}Adjust functions, because they're not being used at all now.

commit message:
I have made some substantial changes to recon-all to make it easier to
maintain. The main change is that mris_make_surfaces has been replaced
with several other binaries (mainly mris_place_surface).
mris_make_surfaces has inputs and outputs that are not very clear; the
code is very difficult to follow and maintain.

I have tested the new stream on combinations of T1 and T1+T2,
conformed and hires, and cross-sectional, base, and longitudinal and
on Buckner40 group age analysis. The new recon-all does not give
identical results to the previous, but they are very close.

Here are some notes on the changes:

- Separate calls to create white.preapac, white, pial, and pial with
  T2/FLAIR (white and pial used to be done in the same call). There
  is now a -white.preaparc flag, which is what the -white flag used to
  control. The -white flag now controls the creation of the white
  surface. The imact of the -white flag is now felt in -autorecon3
  instead of -autorecon2.

- ?h.thickness is created by its own call. Previously, it was created
  at the end of mris_make_surfaces.

- There are new files called autodet.gw.stats.?h.dat which have
  gray/white T1 intensity stats used to place the white and pial
  surfaces on the T1 (created by mris_autodet_gwstats). Previously,
  these stats were recomputed each time mris_make_surfaces run.

- The ?h.cortex.label is created once after white.preaparc. Before it
  was created when white.preaparc and when the white/pial surfaces
  were created.

- There is now a file called ?h.cortex+hipamyg.label. This is the
  corex.label plus vertices adjacent to hippocampus and amygdala; it
  used to place the pial (see below).

- The pial surface is now in the same place as the white in the entire
  medial wall. Previously, it was allowed to float in hippocampus and
  amygdala. In the implementation, the pial is allowed to float in
  hippocampus and amygdala as before (using the cortex+hipamgy label
  above), but when the placement is finished, the vertices in hip and
  amyg are pinned back to the white surface. It was not possible to
  simply freeze the pial in hip/amyg vertices because it would
  adversely affect nearby vertices in entorhinal and parahip.

- The pial created on the T1 is called ?h.pial.T1. If the pial is
  not refined using T2 or FLAIR, then there will be a symoblic link
  from ?h.pial to ?h.pial.T1. If there is refinement, the refined
  surface will be called ?h.pial.{T2,FLAIR} and ?h.pial will be
  a symoblic link to that file.

- Not all mris_make_surfaces options have been implemented in
  mris_place_surfaces.

- When mris_place_surface and mris_autodet_gwstats are run, the inputs
  and outputs are fully specified. The input and output file
  modification times are checked, and the output is not regenerated
  unless an input is younger than the output. The same goes for
  thickness, area, volume, and curv (which are always generated if
  their input files exist). This can be turned off with -force-update.

- One small change in the T2/FLAIR stream is that bbregister is called
  with absolute projection distances rather than relative to the
  thickness since the thickness has not been computed by that time.

commit message:
Extra Unit Tests for VisitCounter (#90)

* Turn on the 'exact' tests in the VisitCounter
These will exercise edge cases not yet implemented in the GPU version

* Adding an AutoCorners test case
This creates simple tetrahedra in the unit cube with the apex at each of the eight corners in turn, and the other vertices lying directly along the edges
The order of the vertices is also permuted through all of the possible orders, to ensure that there is no freak rounding error in the matrix which converts to barycentric co-ordinates

* Add GPU tests to the AutoCorners tests

* Working on test refactoring

* Refactoring the visit counter tests

* Copying the edge case detection from the CPU side
This has fixed the mixed precision GPU implementation, but made the single precision case worse

* Remove redundant test method

* Adding more tests, using the basic 'autocorner' idea, but scaling the tetrahedron and target image

* Adding consistency check, to see if the inside/outside decision stays the same as a single tetrahedron is made larger

% md = fast_dilate(m,<ndilations>,<erodeflag>,<flag2d>)
%
% Dilate or erode a binary mask.
%  m - input binary mask
%  ndilations - number of dilations (or erodes), def=1
%  erodeflag - erode instead of dilate
%  flag2d - perform dilation or erosion in 2d only.
%
% Algorithm: a single dilation consists of setting a voxel to 1 if
% it has a neighbor that is 1. The neighborhood is 3x3x3, unless
% flag2d=1, then 3x3x1. Dilation and erosion are reversible only
% if there are no edge effects.

commit message:
COMP: Allow building with compliers that generate many warnings

Modern compilers on new platforms often provide many more warnings than older compilers
for example the gcc 7.5.0 compiler warnings about falling through switch statements
without explicit breaks on every case.  This desired fallthrough behavior causes false
compiler errors with "-Werror" turned on.  The WARNING_AS_ERROR option allows temporarily
disabling warnings as errors to allow a more gradual move to supporting new compilers.

commit message:
function [F, dof1, dof2, ces] = fast_fratiow(beta,X,rvar,C,nacf,nacfmap)
% [F dof1 dof2 ces] = fast_fratiow(beta,X,rvar,C,<nacf>,<nacfmap>)
%
% beta - GLM regression coefficients from fast_glmfitw
% rvar - residual error variance from GLM from fast_glmfitw
% X - design matrix used with fast_glmfit.
% nacf is the noise autocorrelation function used with fast_glmfit.
%  Can have multiple columns. If so, need nacfmap.
% nacfmap is a map of which column of nacf is to be applied
%   to which voxels in y as used with fast_glmfitw. Voxels that
%   have nacfmap=0 will be treated as white.
%
% F - F-ratio. The Fsig is not computed here. Use:
%   Fsig = FTest(dof1, dof2, F, dof2max);
% ces - contrast effect size = C*beta.
%
% See also: fast_glmfitw, FTest, fast_glmfit, fast_fratio.

commit message:
o MRIScomputeSecondFundamentalForm(...)
o MRIScomputeSecondFundamentalFormAtVertex(...)

For ill-conditioned events at a vertex when computing the
second order fundamental form, individual K and H curvatures
can greatly exceed the current surface Kmax and Hmax, producing
large outliers. This skews statistics on these surfaces.

The correction limits the vertex K and H to, in this case,
the current surface Kmax and Hmax.

Enabling the use of the CUDA stream API, for asynchronous use of the GPU
This is optional, and defaults are set so that things are synchronous
As part of this, we have the option to provide page locked buffers to the transfer routines
If you want to use another stream, you'd better provide a buffer dedicated to it, or your program will misbehave
Finally, CUDA_CHECK_KERNEL is now CUDA_CHECK_ERROR, since always synchronising after each kernel sort of defeats the point of this exercise

%
% Determine the file specification (fspec), stem (fstem), and format
% (fmt) from the given file string.
%
% A specification is the name of a file as it could exist on disk. The
% specification has the form fstem.fmt, where fmt can be mgh, mgz,
% bhdr, or img. fstring can be either an fspec or fstem.
%
% If fstring is an fspec, then the format is determined from the
% extension.
%
% If fstring is an fstem, then the format is determined by finding a
% file on disk named fstem.fmt. The formats are searched in the
% following order: mgh, mgz, bhdr, or img. The search order is only
% important when there are multiple files that would have met the
% criteria, then only the first one is chosen. If no such file is
% found, then empty strings are returned.

commit message:
These were some substantial changes involving coordinate
transformations.

I found that some functions that Tosa wrote (surfaceRASFromVoxel_() and
voxelFromSurfaceRAS_()) were incorrect in that they only worked for
conformed/coronally-oriented volumes. Tosa's "surface" space is
supposed to be "tkregister" or "Volume RAS" space, so I changed them
to use  MRIxfmCRS2XYZtkreg().

While I was at it, I changed extract_i_to_r() to use
MRIxfmCRS2XYZ(). This consequently affects extract_r_to_i(). It also
changes MRIgetVoxelToRasXform() since that is #defined to
extract_i_to_r(). So, it affects lots of stuff.

  1. for backward compatibility, both TAG_GCAMORPH_GEOM_PLUSSHEAR and TAG_GCAMORPH_GEOM are read and written;

% X = fast_fourier_reg(period,nf,<TR>,<nharmonics>)
%
% Creates a fourier regression matrix.
%
% period - stimulation period in seconds (see TR)
% nf - number of frames
% TR - TR in seconds. If not present or empty, TR=1s
% nharmonics - number of harmonics to add. If not present
%   or empty, nharmonics=0.
%
% X - matrix with nf rows and 2*(1+nharmonics) columns.
%  The first  column is the sine   at the fundamental.
%  The second column is the cosine at the fundamental.
%
% Note: this really has nothing to do with the fast fourier

commit message:
Renames (actually copies) input dicom files to a new name that
takes the form outbase-SSS-IIIII.dcm. The output can be used
with dcmdir-info-mgh.

Example:

dicom-rename dicomdir/* --o mydicoms/bert

This will find all the dicoms in dicomdir/*, and rename them to
mydicoms/bert-SSS-IIIII.dcm, where SSS is the series number (dicom tag
20,11) and IIIII is the image number (dicom tag 20,13). The series
number and image number are padded with zeros to make them 3 or 5
digits long. Note: does not actually rename the dicom file; it just
copies it to a new name (ie, it will not delete the input file(s)).

It is ok if input files are not dicom. The script will only use the
files in the list that are dicom.

This script is especially useful when copying data from a Siemens CD
where the file names are often uninterpretable.


See also cp-dicom, dcmdir-info-mgh, mri_probedicom, unpacksdcmdir

commit message:
This GCA was created to perform MRF on the samseg crisp segmentation
to help refine the boundaries. The GCA was created by:

1. Running the manual seg subjects through v6 recon-all to create the
orig.mgz (maybe other outputs needed by xcerebralseg below)

2. Running each orig.mgz through samseg to create the
bias corrected image, the segmentation, and samseg.talairach.lta

3. Linking samseg.talairach.lta to mri/transforms

4. Merging the manual labels (seg_edited10.mgz) with the extacerebral
segmentation from crispSementation (to create seg+xcer.mgz):

xcerebralseg --s $s --o seg+xcer.mgz --m seg_edited10.mgz \
    --seg1 samseg/orig_crispSegmentation.nii \
    --srcvol samseg/orig_biasCorrected.nii --no-pons --no-vermis

5. Train with

mri_ca_train  -prior_spacing 2 -node_spacing 4 -mask seg+xcer.mgz \
  -parc_dir seg+xcer.mgz -xform samseg.talairach.lta \
  -T1 samseg.talairach.lta $subjectlist $trggca

commit message:
Reduce fixture load time and use fewer fixtures.

- Reduce pytest startup time by deferring mini DrugBank SD
  record->molecule converstion until needed in the test.

- Reduce number of mini DrubBank records tested (preserving coverage).

The fixture system loads all of the fixtures even if only one method
was selected for a test. The get_mini_drug_bank() fixture loader
parsed all the records (SDF -> native toolkit - topology Molecule),
which took time. This made it tedious to focus on just one test.

The new version reads mini DrugBank as a set of bytestring records,
with a way for the test case to turn the record into a molecule using
the toolkit under test.

Further, many of the mini DrugBank test cases were not needed. The
subset chosen here preserves basic branch coverage found by
off_coverage's "func-pairs".

commit message:
[qcschema roundtripping] Restructured `from_qcschema` around two known types of inputs

We now understand clearly that we wish to support creating OpenFF
molecule objects from the following QC* objects:
- dataset entry objects, such as OptEntry
    - has hydrogen-mapped CMILES in 'attributes'
- molecule record objects, which are QCElemental Molecules
- QCElemental Molecules that did not originate from a database, but have
hydrogen-mapped CMILES attached, perhaps from `Molecule.to_qcschema`
    - has hydrogen-mapped CMILES in 'extras'

This restructuring more explicitly maps to these two cases.

Resolve warnings emitted by Sphinx (#847)

* github.com/openforcefield/openforcefield -> openff-toolkit

* Fixed or removed all dead links in release history

* Updated release history for PR #846

* Updated intersphinx URLs

* Fixed numpydoc warnings related to FrozenMolecule.to_qcschema() method

* Fixed warnings related to Particle.molecule() docstring

* Fixed remaining warnings in molecule.py

* Fixed documentation warnings in topology.py

* Fixed documentation warnings in forcefield.py

* Resolved extraneous documentation warnings from parameters.py

Two classes of docs warnings remain in parameters.py:

1. Warnings related to importing the entire documentation
   of `ParameterAttribute` all over the place
2. Warnings related to trying to import from classes as
   though they were modules:

```
WARNING: autodoc: failed to import class 'ProperTorsionType' from module 'ProperTorsionHandler'; the following exception was raised:
No module named 'ProperTorsionHandler'
```

* Fixed most documentation warnings from toolkits.py

* Fixed documentation warnings re. toolkit_installation_instructions

`ToolkitWrapper` and subclasses' `toolkit_installation_instructions`
method was previously decorated with both @property and @classmethod.
Not only does this cause its docstring to be replaced by that of
@classmethod, it also causes the property to be inaccessible. The method
is now only a @property.

* Fixed documentation warnings from utils.py

* Fixed documentation warnings in standalone rst files

* Fixed `ParameterAttribute` docstring appearing all over docs

New instances of `ParameterAttribute` now have their docstrings
set by an optional argument in their constructor. This prevents
the ParameterAttribute class' docstring from being pasted everwhere
the descriptor is used, and resolves ~255 Sphinx warnings.

* Linted codebase

* Updated changelog

commit message:
Moving to MyST (#871)

* Replace m2r2 with myst

* Remove unnecessary dependencies from docs/environment.yml

* Add some myst typography beautifiers

* Demonstrate linking to API docs with markdown

* Consistently use colons for directives

* Allow MathJax to run on $..$ and $$...$$ blocks

* Use level 2 header in examples readme (fixes warning)

* Convert virtualsites.rst to markdown

* docs/topology.rst -> docs/topology.md

Unfortunately, Sphinx Autodoc, the program we use to parse docstrings
into documentation, is hard-coded to produce RST rather than Markdown.
As a result, using markdown directive syntax for autosummary sections
results in ugly, broken links. A workaround is to continue to use RST
syntax for these sections, but wrap them in the markdown {eval-rst}
directive.

See https://myst-parser.readthedocs.io/en/latest/using/howto.html#use-sphinx-ext-autodoc-in-markdown-files

* Updated new FAQ entry from RST after merge

* Add links to API docs from SMIRNOFF spec

* Update release history

* Lint codebase

commit message:
Standardize toolkit I/O (#1006)

* normalize format name to upper-case

* normalize file format in from_file_obj(). Move .upper() to a common function

* raise an exception when the format isn't supported, rather than returning mols = []

* use a common helper function to map file_format to the OEFormat_*; raise ValueError if not found.

* OpenEye wrapper from_file() now listens to file_format

* in RDKit.from_file_obj(file_format="SMI") save to a local file and use SmilesMolSupplier instead of writing a new SMILES parser

* the RDKit API allows "MOL" as an alias for "SDF" so do the same here.

* forward RDKit's from_file_obj(allow_undefined_stereo) for SDF

* properly change if/elif in format_name test. If from_file_obj(format_name) doesn't exist, raise ValueError

* test the OEChem and RDKit toolkit wrappers have the same file I/O behavior

* check fileobj coordinate handling. Check _cls handling in from_file/from_file_obj

* pulled the SDF parsing into its own method so from_file_obj() could use the same code as from_file()

* add tests for the "smi" to_file()/to_file_obj(), change toolkits to use the same SMILES as to_smiles(); don't include a header line in RDKit

* added more informative error messages when the file_obj is in binary instead of text mode

* normalize the error message when the output format isn't supported

* check for SMILES parse error

* add some basic SMILES tests

* fixed bug where the RDKit SMILES file output didn't include the molecule name

* check for "ethanol" in the SMILES output line. Check that stereochemistry testing works in from_smiles()

* added atom_map test from test_toolkits.py

* black and isort

* the change I made support OEChem to_file() means I don't need temporary_cd()

* add requires_{rdkit,openeye} guards

* improve comments for data file managers. Using "file_obj_manager" instead of "fileobj_manager" for consistency

* added test that the SDF parser could handle two molecules

* test reading two molecules from a SMILES file

* handle RDKit parse failures in SMILES file lines instead of raise an odd exception with the None molecule

* tests for reading multiple structure SDF/SMI files, including skipping error records

* use Chem.ForwardSDMolSuppler instead of Chem.SupplierFromFilename because the format is specified; no need to guess from the filename.

* Added OEChem ifs(filename).IsValid() test to see if the open failed. Raise error if it fails.

* added test that file_format overrides any default guess the toolkit might have

* check OEChem oeofstream(filename).IsValid() and raise OEError on failure

* black cleanup

* added ParseError to  toolkit.utils.__all__

* I should learn to run the tests before committing. They work again.

* added information about issue #1005 / PR #1006

* improved documentation on RDKit SMILES from_file_obj() backwards compability support for 't'ext mode files

* Put information about the changed to_file(file_format="SMI") behaviors: explicit [H]:s for both toolkits, no header line for RDKit

* improved the text (hopefully) concerning the SMILES to_file() changes from PR #1006.

* comment the toolkit wrapper fixture based on feedback at https://github.com/openforcefield/openff-toolkit/pull/1006#discussion_r664963122

* fixed copy&paste error resulting in two tests with the same name.
Fixed the test case that wasn't actually being tested.

* fixed two more cases where copy&paste'd method names weren't updated, shadowing other tests

* black
